chapters.title: Chapter 2: Landmark—Voluntary Consent to Search: Schneckloth and Bumper
chapters.reason: This chapter teaches the core consent doctrines anchored in Schneckloth (totality-of-the-circumstances voluntariness test and no requirement to know the right to refuse) and Bumper (consent invalidated when induced by a claim of legal authority). Excerpts are needed so students can read the Court's formulations and language used in assessing voluntariness and coercion.

chapters.title: Chapter 4: Landmark—Third-Party Consent: Matlock and Progeny
chapters.reason: Matlock establishes the common-authority basis for third-party consent; the chapter's discussion of joint access/control, apparent authority, and limits when a co-occupant objects would materially benefit from the Matlock opinion excerpt to show the Court's reasoning and key terms.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: Landmark—Scope of Consent: Florida v. Jimeno and Related Principles
chapters.reason: Jimeno provides the seminal articulation of the objective reasonableness test for the scope of consent—what a typical reasonable person would have understood. Including the opinion excerpt grounds the chapter's guidance on spatial limits, containers, and interpreting consent language.

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Landmark—Video Evidence and Appellate Factfinding: Scott v. Harris
chapters.reason: Scott v. Harris contains the controlling language about when clear video evidence can 'blatantly contradict' a party's version of events and thereby control appellate factfinding. The chapter should include the excerpt so readers can see the standard and its application to recorded evidence.
